summary: A 1936 pole platform and tent, then a 1940 40-ft pole L-4 tower on the Idaho-Montana border; removed in the 1950s, with concrete piers and eye hooks reported.

facts.design: 40-ft pole tower with L-4 cab (1940), after a 1936 pole platform and tent
facts.status_note: Removed or destroyed in the 1950s; concrete piers and embedded eye hooks are the reported remains.

visit.trail_note: Hike-in site, per Idaho Fire Lookouts

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com says the tower was removed; the Forest Lookouts page says destroyed. Both put it in the 1950s.

notes_for_editor: The brief gives three coordinate sets that differ by about 1.6 km (FFLA 48.03776, -116.05013; Idaho Fire Lookouts 48.03962, -116.07145; WestUS 48.0383, -116.0577). No source here settles the point, so the location is unchanged. Idaho's index also lists Elk Ridge entries in Idaho and Shoshone counties; these sources describe the Bonner County site. Both sources date the removal or destruction only to the 1950s, so no event is given for it. Staffing is limited to a 1948 visit-type item and no documented history; the story says so only as the Idaho listing's own statement.
